_name: Reading and writing progression per level
_description: What a book at each level must look like as TEXT: how much of it there is, which punctuation is allowed, which sentence forms and devices are expected. Sourced from the Writing and Grammar Track of CURRICULUM_LEDGER.md (the user-authored Curriculum Ledger is the source of truth) plus the sentence-length caps the book pipeline already used.
_use: Drives the story writer's per-level brief AND the text QA gate, so both sides read from one spec. punctuation and sentence_forms are CUMULATIVE (a level inherits everything below it); devices_new and must_include are what this level adds.
_status: sentences_per_page and words_per_sentence are PROPOSED and need Lynden's confirmation; punctuation, sentence_forms and devices_new come straight from the ledger.

1.name: Ditties
1.note: One short caption-like sentence. No commas, no dialogue.

2.name: First Sounds
devices_new: capital letter for the personal pronoun I
2.note: Full stop and capital are formally taught here — the book must model them perfectly.

3.name: Special Friends
devices_new: question mark
capital letters for people and places
must_include: at least one question somewhere in the book
3.note: Question mark is introduced at this level, so the book should show one.

4.name: Longer Sounds
devices_new: joining two ideas with 'and'
exclamation mark
plural -s / -es
suffixes -ing, -ed, -er (no root change)
must_include: at least one sentence joined with 'and'
4.note: First level where two ideas may share a sentence.

5.name: New Spellings
devices_new: commas in lists
prefix un-
suffixes with root change (hopping, hopped)
must_include: sentences that sequence — the story reads as connected events, not captions
5.note: Sequencing sentences into a short narrative starts here.

6.name: Building Fluency
devices_new: expanded noun phrases (the old wooden door)
coordination with and / but / or / so
subordination with when / if / that / because
apostrophes for contractions (don't, it's)
must_include: at least one expanded noun phrase
at least one sentence using but, or, so, when, if or because
at least two different sentence forms
6.note: Consistent tense throughout is explicitly required from this level.

7.name: Reading Together
devices_new: time adverbials (first, next, then, after that, finally)
apostrophe for singular possession (the dog's bone)
suffix spelling rules (doubling, dropping e, y to i)
must_include: two or three time adverbials in the WHOLE book, placed where the story genuinely moves on — never one per page, which reads like a worksheet
at least one sentence with a subordinate clause
complex sentence structures are expected at this level — not every sentence may be simple
7.note: Ledger: 'Complex sentence structures expected.' A Level 7 book that reads like Level 4 has failed.

8.name: Reading Champion
devices_new: sentence variety: open with a subordinate clause, an -ing word, or a fronted adverbial
time, place and manner adverbials (first, outside, carefully)
progressive tense forms (was running, is jumping)
expanded noun phrases for specificity
must_include: at least one sentence opening with a fronted adverbial, followed by a comma
at least one sentence opening with a subordinate clause or an -ing word
varied sentence openings — no more than half the sentences may start with the hero's name or 'The'
8.note: Reading for meaning, not new GPCs. The writing should carry the level, since the phonics no longer does.
